title: Fermi Paradox
logline: Gus is sure aliens are everywhere because space is huge. Vera asks where they all are, and the silence is the Fermi paradox.
pov: If aliens exist, why so quiet?
description: Billions of stars. Zero calls. Sources and simplifications in the pinned comment.

claims.text: Radio searches for signals from other civilisations began in 1960 (Project Ozma) and have found no confirmed signal.
claims.source: OpenStax, Astronomy 2e, §30.4 The Search for Extraterrestrial Intelligence (openstax.org)

claims.text: The Milky Way contains hundreds of billions of stars.
claims.source: OpenStax, Astronomy 2e, Chapter 25 The Milky Way Galaxy (openstax.org)

claims.text: On average, every star in the Milky Way has at least one planet.
claims.source: Cassan et al. 2012, 'One or more bound planets per Milky Way star from microlensing observations', Nature 481, 167-169

claims.text: The Milky Way is about 13 billion years old; Earth is about 4.5 billion years old.
claims.source: OpenStax, Astronomy 2e, Chapter 25 The Milky Way Galaxy and §7.1 Overview of Our Planetary System (openstax.org)

claims.text: The Fermi paradox is the contradiction between the high estimated chance of alien civilisations and the lack of any evidence for them.

simplifications: 'Not one clear signal' means none confirmed: the 1977 'Wow!' signal was never seen again.
Searches so far cover only a tiny slice of the sky and of radio frequencies, so silence is not proof that nobody is there.
'Most stars have planets' is a survey average, not a count.

lines.text: Space is huge. Aliens must be everywhere.
Maybe. But then, where is everybody?
If they're out there, we'd hear them easily.
We've listened since 1960. Not one clear signal.
lines.spoken: We've listened since nineteen sixty. Not one clear signal.

lines.text: Our galaxy has billions of stars, and most have planets.
And it's billions of years older than Earth.
Big numbers feel like proof. Without evidence, they're just a guess.
So many stars, and total silence. That's the Fermi paradox.
Unless they heard us. And they're hiding.
